name: Piperacillin/tazobactam
route_note: IV infusion every 6–8 hours; extended or continuous infusion is used in many hospitals.

discovery.note: Piperacillin, an anti-pseudomonal ureidopenicillin, was developed in the 1970s; tazobactam is a penicillanic acid sulfone beta-lactamase inhibitor.

tagline: Broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal penicillin combination, a hospital mainstay
summary: Piperacillin/tazobactam pairs an extended-spectrum penicillin with the beta-lactamase inhibitor tazobactam. It covers Pseudomonas aeruginosa, many Enterobacterales, streptococci, methicillin-susceptible staphylococci and anaerobes, and is among the most used empirical antibiotics in hospitals.
mechanism: Piperacillin binds penicillin-binding proteins, particularly PBP3 of Gram-negative bacilli, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis; its polar ureido side chain improves penetration and anti-pseudomonal activity.
Tazobactam irreversibly inhibits many class A beta-lactamases (including TEM, SHV and some CTX-M enzymes), protecting piperacillin. It is weak against AmpC, OXA and carbapenemase enzymes.
uses: Complicated urinary tract infections and sepsis of unknown source

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: The WHO Essential Medicines List begins grouping antibiotics into Access, Watch and Reserve categories; piperacillin/tazobactam is placed in the Watch group.

history.title: Global shortage
history.detail: An explosion at a Chinese active-ingredient plant in late 2016 causes worldwide shortages.

history.title: MERINO trial
history.detail: In ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli or Klebsiella bloodstream infection, piperacillin/tazobactam did not show non-inferiority to meropenem for 30-day mortality (JAMA 2018).

history.title: Acute kidney injury debate
history.detail: Studies such as ACORN compare cefepime with piperacillin/tazobactam; combination with vancomycin remains associated with higher reported AKI rates in observational data.

serious: Haematological toxicity (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) with prolonged use
Acute kidney injury, particularly reported with vancomycin

facts: Piperacillin/tazobactam is classified in the WHO 'Watch' antibiotic group.
It is one of the few beta-lactam combinations with reliable activity against anaerobes as well as Pseudomonas.
